summary: Braxton County Schools argues for preserving E‑Rate affordability, cautions against new conditions that raise costs or burden, and opposes blanket screen‑use mandates. Braxton County Schools argues that while it supports CIPA’s protective purpose, it cannot feasibly extend equivalent filtering to all privately owned devices on its E‑Rate‑funded network, and it highlights the limited funds available for essential network maintenance versus classroom technology upgrades. The comment argues for more flexible post‑commitment adjustments, faster processing, and tighter control of unused Category II budgets, while cautioning against blanket opt‑out mandates and over‑extension of C‑Rate authority. Braxton County Schools urges the FCC to preserve core E‑Rate funding for schools and libraries, evaluate a separate safety‑focused category, reject blanket screen‑time limits, adopt a reasonable‑measures CIPA framework, and streamline consultant and ECF compliance requirements.
